policy_identity.objective: replace the seven ordinary individual income-tax marginal rates while preserving the current-law base and indexed bracket thresholds

post_2026_threshold_rule.rule: retain every current-law filing-status breakpoint and current-law inflation adjustment for each later taxable year

unchanged_tax_parameters: qualified dividend and long-term capital-gain rate schedules
estate, gift, corporate, excise, and other federal taxes
penalty, interest, refund, and collection rules except stated transition relief

interaction_rules.treatment: apply the specified rates through existing marginal bracket layering to taxable ordinary income
retain current-law stacking and preferential rates; ordinary-rate changes affect only the ordinary-income portion and statutory stacking interactions
recompute liability under unchanged current-law credit and AMT rules using the specified ordinary tax liability
no rate, base, threshold, deduction, credit, payroll, corporate, estate, gift, or excise change is specified
no spending instrument is included; H.R. 2247 remains a conditional nonpackage cost note

administration_and_transition.treasury_withholding_tables: Treasury and IRS update wage and pension withholding methods as soon as practicable for wages and payments after enactment.
administration_and_transition.employer_and_payor_transition: Employers and payors may continue the previously published 2026 methods until the mandatory effective date stated in implementing guidance.
administration_and_transition.estimated_tax_transition: No underpayment penalty arises solely from pre-guidance installments calculated under the previously published 2026 schedule when later installments follow implementing guidance.
administration_and_transition.return_and_software_updates: Forms, instructions, e-file schemas, tax software, and IRS systems implement the specified rates for TY2026 returns filed in 2027.
administration_and_transition.effective_date_if_enacted_after_2026_sta: Official scoring must separately identify retroactive liability, withholding catch-up, refund/balance-due, compliance, and feasibility effects; the model does not assume immediate retroactive collection.
administration_and_transition.appropriation: Administrative resources are to be estimated by IRS/JCT/CBO and are not assigned a synthetic amount.

public_warning: This is a complete model scoring specification, not legislation or an official proposal. It fixes duration, filing-status breakpoints, unchanged provisions, interactions, transition, and the budget window so an external scorer can analyze the same policy Taxlane modeled. Legislative Counsel text and official scoring remain outstanding.
